Interactive geography uses the Equal Earth projection with Natural Earth boundaries.

Equal Earth projection:
Šavrič, Patterson & Jenny (2018), The Equal Earth map projection.
UN initiative on equal-area maps:
https://www.un.org/osaa/en/news/victory-africa-un-votes-resolution-correct-map
Mathematical reference:
https://proj.org/en/stable/operations/projections/eqearth.html
https://github.com/d3/d3-geo/blob/main/src/projection/equalEarth.js

The projection follows the equal-area approach promoted by the UN; country boundary
data is from Natural Earth. This website is not an official United Nations map.
The illustrations are navigation aids, not the owner's saved travel destinations.

Current interactive asset: geography-data.js, 177 country/area features.
Uniform scale 176, origin [500,250], SVG viewBox 0 0 1000 500.

Dataset: Natural Earth 1:110m Admin 0 - Countries
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/master/geojson/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.geojson
Project: https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector
License: Public domain; no permission or attribution required.
Terms: https://www.naturalearthdata.com/about/terms-of-use/
Accessed: 2026-10-17

Legacy static asset retained for compatibility: world-map.svg
Projection: Equirectangular / plate carree, longitude [-180,180], latitude [-90,90].
SVG viewBox: 0 0 1000 500
x=(longitude+180)/360*1000; y=(90-latitude)/180*500.
Each of the 177 source country features is retained as a path, including polygons and holes.
Coordinates are rounded to 0.01 SVG units. The original antimeridian split is retained.
The full-width south-pole edge belongs to Antarctica, closing the polygon at y=500.
